speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have been experiencing intense itching and developing red bumps on your thigh and other parts of your body. To help me determine the cause, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any patterns related to heat, sweating, or new clothing?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chigger infestation (Trombiculiasis)

Thank you for the details; the timing of your trip to Miami right before the rash appeared is a significant clue. Given your history of diabetes and the nature of the "red bumps," have you noticed any fluid-filled blisters or a burning sensation rather than just itching?
